company.name: Barbour
company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

company.name: The Arts Club
company.description:
The Arts Club was founded in 1863, to provide a haven for those with a professional or amateur relationship with the Arts, Literature or Sciences, and it has continued to welcome a community of discerning thinkers and thought leaders ever since.

From distinguished art exhibitions to fine dining, live music and an exceptional programme of events, the club remains at the heart of contemporary cultural life in London.

Currently occupying an elegant Mayfair townhouse, the club has included among its members many outstanding figures in the history of art, literature and science. Writers such as Charles Dickens, Wilkie Collins and Thomas Hughes; musicians such as Paolo Tosti, Charles Halle and Franz Liszt; artists such as Frederic Leighton, John Everett Millais, Auguste Rodin and James McNeill Whistler, have all played an integral part in the club’s history.

It continues to be a home away from home for many such creatives, entrepreneurs and innovative thinkers, with the principal areas of interest among members being art, architecture, fashion, film, literature, music, science, and media. It provides a serene space for individuals to come together to meet, exchange ideas, dine and participate in an extensive cultural programme, comprising panel discussions, exhibitions, studio and gallery tours and music performances.

The club’s art collection remains at its core, with temporary exhibitions alongside an extensive permanent collection. Curated by Wedel Art, the exhibitions shown in the Drawing and Ante rooms highlight international trends and contemporary works, and in recent years have included artworks by Frank Bowling, Shara Hughes, Yoni Shonibare, Etel Adnan, Laurie Simmons, Sanlé Sory and Sir Peter Blake. The permanent collection is also curated by Wedel Art and can be seen throughout the club and hotel, featuring artworks by Tomas Saraceno, John Baldessari and John Stezaker, among others.

company.name: Barbour
company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

company.name: Barbour
company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

At the heart and soul of London since 1895 West Ham United is a dynamic, fan-focused football Club constantly moving forward but always with an eye on the past. 
 
Our home at the London Stadium has a capacity of 60,000 making it one of the biggest club Stadia in the country however our tickets are the lowest priced for London based clubs in the Premier League, echoing objectives to create Affordable Family Football.

In April 2019, we opened our brand-new Academy facility based at Chadwell Heath which will help to bring through some of the very best talents in the area, the recent emergence of First Team Players Declan Rice and Ben Johnson are a testament to the work already being done at the Academy. 
 
On the business side, we are continuing to create a Stadium our supporters can call home, with the renaming of the Billy Bonds Stand and Claret and Blue pitch surrounding amongst the latest developments. Additionally, the Club is on target to achieve the Advanced Level of the Premier League’s Equality Standard, whilst also achieving the Disability Confident Leader status which highlights the club’s commitment to Equality and Diversity. 
 
The Club employees a constantly growing workforce of approximately 300 core staff and 500 Foundation and events staff,  and is a truly unique place to work and we are always looking for talented individuals who will thrive in our ambitious organisation.

Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

This year marks a new range of modular rail buffers as Oleo International continues to diversify its products for the Rail sector. Oleo products are designed to protect people and equipment from forces generated either during normal running, or from an impact resulting from equipment failure or operator error. The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

company.name: Barbour
company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

company.description:
We’ve been helping people find insurance for 60 years. With friendly faces in our network of branches, combined with online and telephone services which enable a highly personal service, it’s no wonder we serve over one million people, and employ over 3,000 dedicated people

Our Swinton story began in 1957, when Ken Scowcroft sold his first car insurance policy, for just five pounds. Back then you bought your motor insurance from the ‘man’ at your door, but Ken had a better idea.

By comparing prices from lots of insurance companies, Ken could retain the personal touch and pass on the savings to his customers. In his first year, he sold over 100 policies and Swinton Insurance was born.

By 1964, he’d opened his first high street branch and by 1987, Swinton was a household name, with 200 branches nationwide.

Throughout the years, Swinton has been committed to working hard for our customers, taking the time to listen and going the extra mile, so challenge Swinton to find you a great deal. 

This honest personal approach, inherited from Ken, is still the cornerstone of our business. Today we offer a wide range of insurance products; from car to home, commercial to taxi insurance, plus services like breakdown cover. And we also look for the same qualities in the individuals and companies we work with. 

But it’s our people and their dedication to our customers that make the biggest difference. This is why many people trust us to help protect the things that matter to them.

person.headline: Hospitality Professional & Managing Director at Comptoir Group PLC

company.name: Comptoir Group
company.description:
Comptoir Group Plc was founded by Tony Kitous following his move from Algeria to London when he was just  aged 18.  Tony’s love for traditional homeland food shaped his vision to share Lebanese food.  The group has expanded over the years but the values have remained the same.
 
The heart and soul of the Company is the team members, most of whom progress their way through the ranks to GM or Head Chefs.  Creating a family environment and providing generous hospitality to every guest is a key ingredient of the business.
 
The Restaurants:
 
Comptoir Libanais translated means ‘Lebanese Counter’ and that summarises the brand.  Everyone is welcome to eat the authentic Lebanese food within a friendly and calm environment.  The interior is created using items frm the Middle East such as the tiles you would see in courtyards through to Grandmother oil cloths, which are used on the chairs.  A section of each restaurant is dedicated to a Souk Market where guests can purchase speciality ingredients, homeware and handmade Moroccan bags.
 
Levant, located in Jason Court, Wigmore Street in the West End and Kenza restaurant can be found in the City within Devonshire Square.  These restaurants prepare and serve food using only traditional mother and grandmother recipes from the Middle East.  Decoration is authentic and traditional beautiful lights and furnishings transport you to Marrakesh.  Both restaurants have entertainment including belly dancing and live music.
 
Tony wanted to share the taste of Shawarma with the United Kingdom and Shawa was born.  The creation of wraps is quite a spectacle, as guests watch the team expertly carve the meat, it also offers rotisserie chicken. Shawa is a fast take-away offering healthy food suitable for everyone.
 
Yalla Yalla joined the family in December 2016.  Located in Oxford Circus, Soho and Greenwich the three restaurants are welcoming and unique in style offering a rustic feel with authentic Lebanese food.
company.description_seo: Welcome to Comptoir Libanais, where you can indulge in the flavours of the Middle East and North Africa. Food shared is a memory made.
company.description_ai: Comptoir Libanais is a Lebanese canteen-style restaurant group offering Middle Eastern and North African dishes such as mezze, grills and tagines. With multiple UK and international locations, it provides dine-in, delivery, private events, catering, a rewards club, gift cards and cookbooks to share its food and culture.

#WeAreBravissimo

Bravissimo is a company that provides a wide choice of lingerie and swimwear in D-L cup. We are passionate about our purpose which is to be the cheerleader for big boobed women and aim to inspire our customers to celebrate their boobs and feel amazing  

Sarah Tremellen set up Bravissimo in 1995 following her own frustrating experiences trying to find pretty bras that fit her. Sarah had been appalled by the lack of choice in her size and was fed up of being offered enormous matronly contraptions more suitable for landing parachutes and being told she could not possibly expect to find gorgeous bras in her size. Adamant that big boobed women like herself deserved a better deal when buying lingerie, Sarah started Bravissimo as a mail order company from her living room. 

Today, we have 25 shops in the UK and an ecommerce operation that supports customers all over the world. We have around 700 employees across the business inclusive of our head office teams based out of Leamington Spa. 

We have some very exciting plans for the future and there has never been a better time to be part of Bravissimo.

company.name: Comptoir Group
company.description:
Comptoir Group Plc was founded by Tony Kitous following his move from Algeria to London when he was just  aged 18.  Tony’s love for traditional homeland food shaped his vision to share Lebanese food.  The group has expanded over the years but the values have remained the same.
 
The heart and soul of the Company is the team members, most of whom progress their way through the ranks to GM or Head Chefs.  Creating a family environment and providing generous hospitality to every guest is a key ingredient of the business.
 
The Restaurants:
 
Comptoir Libanais translated means ‘Lebanese Counter’ and that summarises the brand.  Everyone is welcome to eat the authentic Lebanese food within a friendly and calm environment.  The interior is created using items frm the Middle East such as the tiles you would see in courtyards through to Grandmother oil cloths, which are used on the chairs.  A section of each restaurant is dedicated to a Souk Market where guests can purchase speciality ingredients, homeware and handmade Moroccan bags.
 
Levant, located in Jason Court, Wigmore Street in the West End and Kenza restaurant can be found in the City within Devonshire Square.  These restaurants prepare and serve food using only traditional mother and grandmother recipes from the Middle East.  Decoration is authentic and traditional beautiful lights and furnishings transport you to Marrakesh.  Both restaurants have entertainment including belly dancing and live music.
 
Tony wanted to share the taste of Shawarma with the United Kingdom and Shawa was born.  The creation of wraps is quite a spectacle, as guests watch the team expertly carve the meat, it also offers rotisserie chicken. Shawa is a fast take-away offering healthy food suitable for everyone.
 
Yalla Yalla joined the family in December 2016.  Located in Oxford Circus, Soho and Greenwich the three restaurants are welcoming and unique in style offering a rustic feel with authentic Lebanese food.

company.description:
Toyota's decision to establish a manufacturing operation in Europe was announced in 1989 and Toyota Manufacturing UK was established in December that year.

There are two manufacturing plants in the UK representing a total investment in excess of £2.75 billion and currently approximately 3,000 members (including Agency) are employed. The vehicle manufacturing plant is located at Burnaston in Derbyshire, the engine manufacturing plant is located at Deeside in North Wales. 
The processes at Burnaston include stamping, welding, painting, plastic mouldings and assembly and at Deeside machining, assembly and aluminium casting.
The first car, a Carina E, drove off the Burnaston production line on 16 December 1992. The Avensis replaced the Carina E in 1997 and in 2008 the third generation Avensis was launched. In 1998 a second model, the Corolla, was introduced and in 2001 the new generation Corolla was launched. In 2007, production of Auris, a new Toyota hatchback, started replacing Corolla. Production of the Auris Hybrid, the first full mass-produced hybrid in Europe, began in 2010. 
Toyota is the leading company for hybrid vehicle development, and the new Corolla with its Touring Sports variant is the future of TMUK – the first model to introduce Toyota’s dual hybrid strategy, replaced the Auris when it started to roll off our production lines in January 2019.

person.headline: Senior Global Trade Marketing Coordinator at Barbour

company.name: Barbour
company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

company.name: Oleo International
company.description:
Oleo is an established UK engineering company and a leading expert in energy absorption 

This year marks a new range of modular rail buffers as Oleo International continues to diversify its products for the Rail sector.  By adding modular buffers to its manufacturing programme, Oleo has become one of a few businesses globally with the capability to deliver a complete rail safety solution.

Oleo products are designed to protect people and equipment from forces generated either during normal running, or from an impact resulting from equipment failure or operator error. Traditionally Oleo has achieved this using hydraulic energy absorption systems combined with a gas return spring to give unsurpassed energy dissipation and recovery.

Energy absorption technology generates relatively high forces, even during light impacts, Oleo technology generates lowest possible forces at all impact velocities, which means that the equipment being protected is less likely to suffer from chronic problems such as fatigue, wear, and contact damage and noise. This results in reduced downtime, maintenance, replacement and disposal costs.

Oleo's line of products such as buffers, absorbers, end stops give ultimate protection, reducing impact forces to safe levels in potentially life threatening impacts.

We will work with you to ensure that an energy absorption solution is developed to your specification; we provide solutions – not just products.

Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

Sandicliffe was founded in 1948 by Mr. J R Woodhouse and Mr. T H Barton as a service station on Nottingham Road, Stapleford. The Company became Ford Retail Dealers in 1953 and then by 1955, Ford Car and Commercial Vehicle Distributorships were appointed.

company.name: Barbour
company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

person.headline: Senior Global Trade Marketing Coordinator at Barbour

company.name: Barbour
company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

We develop pioneering technology to elevate life on Earth. Innovating in pursuit of the world's net zero goals. We deliver thermal management solutions to create a better, more sustainable future.

We are a privately owned British aerospace Company known for our pioneering work in air-breathing rocket engine technology, particularly SABRE.  Originally established with a focus on this innovative propulsion system, we have since expanded efforts to include hypersonic propulsion and defence applications and sustainable technology solutions for aerospace and other industries.

The building is also home to Northern Ireland's largest dedicated event and conference space.

company.name: Toyota Motor Manufacturing UK
company.description:
Toyota's decision to establish a manufacturing operation in Europe was announced in 1989 and Toyota Manufacturing UK was established in December that year.

There are two manufacturing plants in the UK representing a total investment in excess of £2.75 billion and currently approximately 3,000 members (including Agency) are employed. The vehicle manufacturing plant is located at Burnaston in Derbyshire, the engine manufacturing plant is located at Deeside in North Wales. 
The processes at Burnaston include stamping, welding, painting, plastic mouldings and assembly and at Deeside machining, assembly and aluminium casting.
The first car, a Carina E, drove off the Burnaston production line on 16 December 1992. The Avensis replaced the Carina E in 1997 and in 2008 the third generation Avensis was launched. In 1998 a second model, the Corolla, was introduced and in 2001 the new generation Corolla was launched. In 2007, production of Auris, a new Toyota hatchback, started replacing Corolla. Production of the Auris Hybrid, the first full mass-produced hybrid in Europe, began in 2010. 
Toyota is the leading company for hybrid vehicle development, and the new Corolla with its Touring Sports variant is the future of TMUK – the first model to introduce Toyota’s dual hybrid strategy, replaced the Auris when it started to roll off our production lines in January 2019. 


See more at: http://www.toyotauk.com/

company.name: Comptoir Group
company.description:
Comptoir Group Plc was founded by Tony Kitous following his move from Algeria to London when he was just  aged 18.  Tony’s love for traditional homeland food shaped his vision to share Lebanese food.  The group has expanded over the years but the values have remained the same.
 
The heart and soul of the Company is the team members, most of whom progress their way through the ranks to GM or Head Chefs.  Creating a family environment and providing generous hospitality to every guest is a key ingredient of the business.
 
The Restaurants:
 
Comptoir Libanais translated means ‘Lebanese Counter’ and that summarises the brand.  Everyone is welcome to eat the authentic Lebanese food within a friendly and calm environment.  The interior is created using items frm the Middle East such as the tiles you would see in courtyards through to Grandmother oil cloths, which are used on the chairs.  A section of each restaurant is dedicated to a Souk Market where guests can purchase speciality ingredients, homeware and handmade Moroccan bags.
 
Levant, located in Jason Court, Wigmore Street in the West End and Kenza restaurant can be found in the City within Devonshire Square.  These restaurants prepare and serve food using only traditional mother and grandmother recipes from the Middle East.  Decoration is authentic and traditional beautiful lights and furnishings transport you to Marrakesh.  Both restaurants have entertainment including belly dancing and live music.
 
Tony wanted to share the taste of Shawarma with the United Kingdom and Shawa was born.  The creation of wraps is quite a spectacle, as guests watch the team expertly carve the meat, it also offers rotisserie chicken. Shawa is a fast take-away offering healthy food suitable for everyone.
 
Yalla Yalla joined the family in December 2016.  Located in Oxford Circus, Soho and Greenwich the three restaurants are welcoming and unique in style offering a rustic feel with authentic Lebanese food.

company.name: Barbour
company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

Our journey began in 1987 by selling end of line sports products directly to customers in the UK. Unlike other online retailers, we don't do discount codes or promotions - just your favourite brands all with up to 65% less than RRP.

Our Mission = Big Brands  Low Price Direct to you

At MandM we’re proud to be different.

We want to give you the biggest brands at the lowest prices you'll find.

How do we do it?
The answer is simple - we buy directly from brands, licensees and suppliers.
Just like you, we're always hunting for a bargain.

Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust (CNWL) has almost 9,200 staff providing integrated healthcare to a third of London's population, Milton Keynes, Surrey and areas beyond.

We provide a wide range of services to treat people with a a variety of health needs, including common physical health problems, long-term conditions, mental health, learning disabilities, eating disorders, addictions and sexual health. We are here to provide support for people through every stage of life.

Our catchment area covers a range of vibrant and diverse communities, with over 100 first languages spoken, ranging from areas of deprivation to areas of affluence. Founded in 1921, we created the world’s first thermostatic shower valve and we have been leading the way ever since. Over the past 100 years, the business has grown exponentially. company.name: Barbour
company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

company.name: Belzona
company.description:
Belzona is a global leader in manufacturing repair composites and protective coatings for industrial machinery and equipment.

Since 1952, Belzona has empowered a wide range of industries including steel, oil & gas, power generation, mining, water, chemical processing, and marine to protect and restore critical assets against abrasion, erosion, corrosion, pitting corrosion, galvanic corrosion, chemical attack and mechanical damage.

Our innovative solutions include high temp epoxy systems, industrial coatings, metal bonding compounds, and metal to metal adhesive technologies designed for long lasting preventative maintenance, emergency repair, and structural reinforcement. Applications include pump repair, pipe wrapping, pipe wraps, corrosion prevention systems, shimming and chocking solutions, and concrete repair.

Belzona products are used to repair and protect pipework, tanks, pumps, structural steel, and concrete assets. Our systems are widely used for flange and pipeline corrosion protection, as well as rebuilding worn components exposed to extreme temperatures and aggressive environments. We also provide solutions for sealing, rebuilding and protecting equipment suffering from wear, corrosion and erosion.

Available through a global network of Distributors, supported by headquarters in the UK, USA, Canada and Thailand, we provide 24-hour technical support and on-site assistance. Our engineered solutions are designed to reduce downtime, extend asset life, and minimise maintenance and replacement costs while supporting sustainable asset management.

All solutions are backed by international accreditations and a proven track record in performance across demanding industrial environments.

For more information, visit www.belzona.com

company.name: Harris + Hoole
company.description:
Harris + Hoole is a chain of speciality coffee shops made up of experienced, passionate coffee lovers. We pour hours of training in to bringing you a better cup of coffee.

We believe that everyone should be able to enjoy better coffee so we serve premium coffee served by highly-trained baristas wherever you see us!

"Harris + Hoole" is a funny name for a coffee shop. Sounds more like a name for a small town firm of solicitors! But in actual fact, the names hail back to the very first days on London's coffee scene, as captured in the diary of Samuel Pepys in 1664:
The excerpt:

"Feb. 3d, 1664. In Covent Garden to-night, going to fetch home my wife, I stopped at the great Coffee-house there, where I never was before: Where Dryden the poet (I knew at Cambridge), and all the wits of the town, and Harris the player, and Mr Hoole of our College. And had I had time then, or could at other times, it will be good coming thither, for there, I perceive, is very witty and pleasant discourse."

So there you go. We reckon it's pretty cool that 400 years on people are still being brought together by great coffee. It's a tradition we are proud to be part of, and if Mr. Pepys were around today we very much hope he'd pop in for a cup.

Like what you've read? Think Harris + Hoole could be just the place for you? We're constantly on the lookout for top talent to be part of our dream team.

This year marks a new range of modular rail buffers as Oleo International continues to diversify its products for the Rail sector.  By adding modular buffers to its manufacturing programme, Oleo has become one of a few businesses globally with the capability to deliver a complete rail safety solution.

Oleo products are designed to protect people and equipment from forces generated either during normal running, or from an impact resulting from equipment failure or operator error. Traditionally Oleo has achieved this using hydraulic energy absorption systems combined with a gas return spring to give unsurpassed energy dissipation and recovery.

Energy absorption technology generates relatively high forces, even during light impacts, Oleo technology generates lowest possible forces at all impact velocities, which means that the equipment being protected is less likely to suffer from chronic problems such as fatigue, wear, and contact damage and noise. This results in reduced downtime, maintenance, replacement and disposal costs.

Oleo's line of products such as buffers, absorbers, end stops give ultimate protection, reducing impact forces to safe levels in potentially life threatening impacts.

Our Swinton story began in 1957, when Ken Scowcroft sold his first car insurance policy, for just five pounds. Back then you bought your motor insurance from the ‘man’ at your door, but Ken had a better idea.

By comparing prices from lots of insurance companies, Ken could retain the personal touch and pass on the savings to his customers. In his first year, he sold over 100 policies and Swinton Insurance was born.

By 1964, he’d opened his first high street branch and by 1987, Swinton was a household name, with 200 branches nationwide.

Throughout the years, Swinton has been committed to working hard for our customers, taking the time to listen and going the extra mile, so challenge Swinton to find you a great deal. 

This honest personal approach, inherited from Ken, is still the cornerstone of our business. Today we offer a wide range of insurance products; from car to home, commercial to taxi insurance, plus services like breakdown cover. And we also look for the same qualities in the individuals and companies we work with. 

But it’s our people and their dedication to our customers that make the biggest difference. This is why many people trust us to help protect the things that matter to them.

company.name: Barbour
company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.

company.description:
At Minster Care Group, we are committed to redefining elderly care in the UK through compassionate, high-quality, and person-centred care.

As a leading UK care home provider, we offer residential, dementia, nursing, respite, and palliative care, tailored to meet each individual’s unique needs. With the UK’s rapidly ageing population, the demand for quality senior living and long-term care solutions continues to grow, and our mission is to meet that demand with care homes across the UK that prioritise dignity, comfort, and independence. 

PERSON CENTRED ELDERLY CARE 
We specialise in person-centred care planning, recognising that every individual has unique medical, emotional, and lifestyle needs. Our tailored approach ensures residents receive individualised elderly care support, promoting independent living, wellbeing, and quality of life.

SAFE AND SUPPORTIVE CARE HOMES 
Our care homes across the UK are designed to offer safe, homely environments for elderly residents, combining professional care with a warm, community-led atmosphere. We emphasise senior wellbeing, mental health support, and social engagement, helping residents lead active and meaningful lives.

SPECIALIST CARE 
Our highly trained teams provide expert support in:
Dementia care and memory care services
24-hour nursing care for elderly residents
Short-term respite care for families and caregivers
End-of-life and palliative care support

At Minster Care Group, our foundation is built on family values, respect, and integrity. These principles guide how we deliver quality care home services, support our teams, and create environments where residents feel safe, valued, and at home.

company.name: Hawes and Curtis
company.description:
Hawes & Curtis is a quintessentially British brand specialising in fine tailoring and accessories for men and women. Founded in 1913 by Ralph Hawes & George Frederick Curtis, Hawes & Curtis has since become the go-to brand for British classics whilst continuing to deliver the promise of exceptional quality, innovation and outstanding value. These values are now synonymous with the Hawes & Curtis name. 

Hawes & Curtis, a Jermyn street shirtmaker for more than 100 years, is proud of its rich heritage.  Since the first store opened in the Piccadilly Arcade, Hawes & Curtis has had many distinguished clients through its doors, including the Duke of Windsor, Lord Mountbatten, Fred Astaire and Cary Grant. As a result of Hawes & Curtis’ commitment to impeccable service and product excellence, the brand has been awarded four Royal Warrants. Officially granted to Hawes & Curtis in 1922 was the Royal Warrant of HRH the Prince of Wales, followed by the Royal Warrant of HRH King George VI in 1938. In 1948 Hawes & Curtis received a third Royal Warrant appointed by HRH King George VI and HRH the Duke of Edinburgh awarded a fourth Royal Warrant in 1957. 

Hawes & Curtis currently has 25 stores in the UK and a store in Germany . Hawes & Curtis’ flagship store remains in the heart of London on Jermyn Street, famous for its resident shirtmakers.

company.name: Belzona
company.description:
Belzona is a global leader in manufacturing repair composites and protective coatings for industrial machinery and equipment.

Since 1952, Belzona has empowered a wide range of industries including steel, oil & gas, power generation, mining, water, chemical processing, and marine to protect and restore critical assets against abrasion, erosion, corrosion, pitting corrosion, galvanic corrosion, chemical attack and mechanical damage.

Our innovative solutions include high temp epoxy systems, industrial coatings, metal bonding compounds, and metal to metal adhesive technologies designed for long lasting preventative maintenance, emergency repair, and structural reinforcement. Applications include pump repair, pipe wrapping, pipe wraps, corrosion prevention systems, shimming and chocking solutions, and concrete repair.

Belzona products are used to repair and protect pipework, tanks, pumps, structural steel, and concrete assets. Our systems are widely used for flange and pipeline corrosion protection, as well as rebuilding worn components exposed to extreme temperatures and aggressive environments. We also provide solutions for sealing, rebuilding and protecting equipment suffering from wear, corrosion and erosion.

Available through a global network of Distributors, supported by headquarters in the UK, USA, Canada and Thailand, we provide 24-hour technical support and on-site assistance. Our engineered solutions are designed to reduce downtime, extend asset life, and minimise maintenance and replacement costs while supporting sustainable asset management.

All solutions are backed by international accreditations and a proven track record in performance across demanding industrial environments.

For more information, visit www.belzona.com

company.name: Barbour
company.description:
The Barbour story began in 1894 in South Shields in the North East of England. Founder John Barbour began supplying oilskins and other garments to protect the growing community of sailors, fishermen and dockers. These first weather resistant items quickly established Barbour’s reputation for innovation and quality. Today, Barbour remains a fifth generation family business. Under the leadership of Chairman Dame Margaret Barbour, Barbour has grown into a lifestyle brand sold in over 55 countries worldwide including Europe, the US and Asia offering a wardrobe of stylish functional clothing, footwear and accessories inspired by the unique values of the British countryside.  The iconic Barbour Bedale and Barbour Beaufort wax jackets continue to be made by hand in the factory in South Shields. Barbour International, the collection for men and women inspired by Barbour’s motorcycle heritage established in 1936, is now a separate stand alone brand with its own identity. 
 
In 2020, Barbour launched Wax for Life, an overarching name for all of Barbour’s wax services designed to encourage customers to extend the life of their wax garments.  Wax for Life includes re-waxing and repairs (first introduced in 1921) and Barbour Re-Loved an upcycling circularity initiative.  Each year over 70,000 wax garments are sent back to Barbour globally to be repaired, rewaxed or altered.
